newsitem.title: CANADA: Suncor climbs amid takeover rumors.
newsitem.headline: Suncor climbs amid takeover rumors.

text.p: Shares in Canadian integrated oil company Suncor Inc climbed to new year highs on the Toronto and American stock exchanges on Monday as rumors circulated that it could be the target of a takeover bid.
The company, however, downplayed the risk of a hostile play, saying low trading volumes and high prices left little chance of a bid.
Suncor shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange surged C$1.40 to C$60.30 in moderate trade of 50,262 shares. The stock has gained 14 percent since November 18.
The company's American Stock Exchange shares were up 2-7/8 to 45-3/8 with just 500 shares changing hands.

Recent big gains for Suncor, which operates a major oil sands mine and plant in northern Alberta, conventional oil and gas business in western Canada and refining and marketing in Ontario, baffled analysts, who said they could detect no other reason for the jump.
"I didn't think you would see this stock at this price for 12 months," said one industry analyst, who asked not to be named.
Suncor last week announced a major increase in capital spending dedicated to all three divisions, but the new spending was factored into the stock price at the time, he said.
Industry sources said Gulf Canada Resources Ltd, which had served notice it was in the hunt for an acquisition, was a potential suitor.

Gulf's success with the Athabasca Oil Sands Trust, a royalty trust set up last year based on an interest in the Syncrude Canada oil sands project, was said to have provided impetus to consider following suit with Suncor's operations.
Athabasca's price has doubled from its initial public offering of C$10 a unit.
But Gulf spokesman John Sparks said on Monday that the size of Suncor -- which has a market capitalization of more than C$3.3 billion -- likely placed it out of Gulf's reach.
"You can discount that (rumor) heavily," Sparks said.
Asked if the concept of a Suncor takeover was considered by Gulf, he said: "I don't think all that seriously."

Cash-rich Shell Canada Ltd, which competes with Suncor in the Ontario gasoline market and is studying its own oil sands lease in northern Alberta, Lease 13, was also mentioned as potentially interested in Suncor.
Shell is searching for a mining industry partner to use new technology for extracting oil from the sands.

Canadian competition regulators would be forced to scrutinize any move that gave one company more than 40 percent of the gasoline market in Ontario, Canada's most populous province, analysts and industry sources said.
Shell vice-president Ron Blakely, citing the company's policy of not commenting on speculation, said, "That's a new one on me."

Suncor spokesman John Rogers said the takeover speculation likely resulted from stock market players searching for a reason for the stock price jump, which has left most analyst projections in the dust.

"When you're a public company, there's always the possibility that you could be a takeover target. But on the other hand, the stock has been moving, rather dramatically I might add, with very low volumes."
((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
